title: Fine early, wrong by the end of the day
description: All eight carrier cut-offs are forecast short, outbound backlog breaches the TOP of its band in the later shifts but not the current one, and the end-of-day target is missed. The backlog ceiling and the end-of-day target both clear - and the model pays for it by pushing the backlog through the BOTTOM of the band, breaking two tiers that were clean before the solve. That trade is legal because `ob_bl_min` sits below `ob_bl_max` and `eod_max` in the ladder. It also exercises the now/later shift split, which the engineered set barely touches: seven of the eight breach in the later partition only, `ib_then_eod` being the exception.

title: Four families at once, and it cannot fix them all
description: Carrier cut-off risk, outbound backlog high in BOTH shift partitions, the end-of-day target and the returns ceiling all breached on the same day. Every one of them is reduced, none is cleared, and the returns ceiling is made eighteen times worse to buy that relief - it is the lowest operational tier, so it is what the ladder spends. Ends on `limited_by = cross_trained_people`: the model moved everyone it could and still fell short.

title: Four families at once, and the trade it makes to get there
description: The contrast case to 90073, and held in reserve - the report does not show it. Cut-off risk, outbound backlog BELOW its band, the end-of-day floor and the returns ceiling all live at once. It ends on `limited_by = resolved`, so the model never hits a ceiling, but that is not the same as fixing the day: the returns breach clears outright and cut-off risk drops by two thirds, while both backlog-too-low tiers and the end-of-day floor are driven further down. The model ships harder to make the deadlines and accepts a thinner backlog as the price.
